name: Ru glaze (a pale blue-green celadon, opalescent, over a buff stoneware body)

diffuseAlbedo.source: National Palace Museum, 故瓷017851, photograph 汝窯_青瓷無紋水仙盆.png (CC BY 4.0); MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py derive_ru
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: The median of the basin's lit outside wall, face on (pixels 1100..1500 x 1350..1500), relative to the photograph's own white (its 99.5th percentile of lightness, the rim's white edge where the glaze runs thin, taken as L* 100).

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/low-iron-glass.json (1.523 for soda-lime float); a ceramic glaze is a soda-lime-alumina-silica glass of about the same index

porosity.derivation: a fired glaze has no open pores

wettingDepth.derivation: with no pores, nothing wets its body

grain.note: The bubbles that make the glaze's sheen soft.

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.source: 汝窯_青瓷無紋水仙盆.png; MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py derive_ru
toneSpread.derivation: The standard deviation of ln(lightness) over the same lit wall: a glaze even to the eye.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
